text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kenya recognises the new regime in Zaire led by rebel leader Laurent Kabila.
- Kenyan troops are deployed around Kapsowar Trading Centre in Marakwet, Rift Valley, as part of a major security operation to retrieve illegal firearms and flush out cattle rustlers.
- Voter registration ahead of general elections later this year begins countrywide.
- Charity Ngilu, of opposition party Democratic Party tells her chairman Mwai Kibaki that she will challenge him for the party presidency ahead of the general elections.
- Official opposition leader Michael Kijana Wamalwa calls for the public destruction of all old generation national identity cards, claiming they could be used to rig polls.
- Today is the official deadline for hawkers to get out of Nairobi streets to areas allocated for them by the city council.
- Prominent central province politician Simon Kuria Kanyingi says he will not defect from the ruling party despite pressure from the opposition.
- A man returns from a journey to find his 11-year old son burning and his hands tied to a bedpost for allegedly stealing five shillings from his uncle.
- Tensions stemming from the pressures of new alignments are quickly becoming apparent in the region, following Zaire's takeover by Laurent Kabila.
- Tanzanians will soon issue national identity cards following the final selection of the company to prepare the document.

- Belgium resumes work on Kenya's controversial munitions factory after receiving adequate guarantees from the government that the bullets from the plant would not be exported to the great lakes region.
